common_mistakes: Landing with locked knees or stiff legs.
Using a box that is too high, compromising form.
Letting the knees cave inward upon landing.
Rushing the reset between jumps.

name: Squat to Cross Body Knee Strike
description: A dynamic bodyweight exercise combining a standard squat with a rotational knee strike, keeping hands in a defensive guard position to engage the core and legs.
breathing_technique: Inhale as you squat down; exhale forcefully as you stand up and perform the cross-body twist.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding your hands in front of your chest/chin in a guard position.
Engage your core and lower into a squat, keeping your chest upright.
Descend until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
Drive through your heels to return to a standing position.
As you rise, explosively lift your right knee toward your chest.
Simultaneously twist your torso to bring your left elbow across to meet the right knee.
Return the right leg to the floor and reset your squat stance.
Immediately perform the next squat repetition.
On the next rise, twist to bring your right elbow to your left knee.
Continue alternating sides with each repetition, keeping hands up throughout.
form_tips: Keep your hands held high near your chin or chest throughout the entire movement.
Focus on rotating your torso to make the connection, not just dropping your arm.
Exhale sharply as you drive the knee up and twist.
Maintain a steady rhythm and do not let your knees collapse inward during the squat.
common_mistakes: Dropping the hands or letting arms swing loosely.
Rounding the back during the squat phase.
Leaning forward too much to force the elbow-knee contact.
Twisting the hips excessively instead of the torso.

name: Dumbbell Incline Front Raise with Chest Support
description: A variation of the dumbbell front raise performed prone on an incline bench for chest support. This setup isolates the anterior deltoids by minimizing momentum and reducing upper trap involvement.
breathing_technique: Exhale as you raise the dumbbell, inhale as you lower it with control.
steps: Set an adjustable bench to a low incline (30-45 degrees).
Lie prone on the bench with your chest supported, head slightly over the top edge.
Hold one dumbbell with both hands, palms facing each other, arms extended towards the floor.
Allow the dumbbell to hang straight down, maintaining a slight bend in your elbows.
Engage your core and, keeping your arms mostly straight, raise the dumbbell forward and upward.
Continue raising until your arms are parallel to the floor or slightly higher.
Pause briefly at the top, focusing on the contraction in your front deltoids.
Slowly and with control, lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Ensure smooth, deliberate movement throughout the entire repetition.
form_tips: Maintain a stable torso with full chest support on the bench.
Avoid using momentum or arching your back during the lift.
Keep a slight, consistent bend in your elbows throughout the movement.
Focus on initiating the movement from your front shoulders.
Control the eccentric (lowering) phase for increased muscle engagement.
common_mistakes: Using excessive weight, which compromises proper form.
Lifting the hips or arching the back off the bench for leverage.
Swinging the dumbbell up using momentum instead of muscle control.
Shrugging the shoulders excessively, over-engaging the upper trapezius.
Dropping the weight too quickly on the descent, losing tension.

name: Curl-up
description: A spine-sparing core exercise that targets the abdominals by lifting the head and shoulders while maintaining a neutral lumbar arch.
breathing_technique: Exhale as you lift your head and shoulders; inhale as you lower back down.
steps: Lie on your back with one leg straight and the other knee bent.
Place your hands underneath your lower back to support the natural arch.
Raise your head and shoulders slightly off the floor as a rigid unit.
Imagine your head and neck are locked; do not tuck your chin.
Hold the top position for a brief pause while bracing your core.
Slowly lower your upper body back to the floor.
Complete the desired reps, then switch the leg position.
Maintain steady breathing throughout the hold.
Ensure your elbows stay on the floor or slightly lifted.
form_tips: Do not flatten your lower back against your hands.
Focus on lifting with your abs, not straining your neck.
Keep the movement small; you only need to clear the floor slightly.
Imagine a string pulling your chest straight up to the ceiling.
common_mistakes: Curling the neck forward (chin-to-chest).
Lifting too high and flattening the lumbar spine.
Holding the breath during the exertion.
Performing the movement too fast.

name: Romanian Chair Sit-Up (Weighted)
description: A core-strengthening exercise performed seated on a bench, using a barbell anchored at the feet for stability while leaning back to engage the abdominals and hip flexors.
breathing_technique: Inhale as you lean back; exhale forcefully as you sit up.
steps: Sit on the edge of a flat bench with your feet hooked under a heavy barbell for stability.
Clasp your hands in front of your chest or across your shoulders.
Engage your core and keep a straight spine.
Lean your torso back slowly, extending at the hips.
Lower yourself until you feel a strong stretch in the abs, keeping tension.
Pause briefly at the point of maximum tension.
Contract your abs to pull your torso back up to the vertical starting position.
Avoid using momentum or jerking your body forward.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Ensure the barbell is heavy enough to counterbalance your weight.
form_tips: Keep your back straight; do not round your spine excessively.
Control the descent; do not drop back quickly.
Focus on using your abs to pull up, not just your hip flexors.
Ensure your feet are securely hooked to prevent tipping.
common_mistakes: Rounding the back and straining the neck.
Using momentum to swing back up.
Going back too far and hyperextending the lower back.
Relying entirely on hip flexors rather than abdominals.
